title: Introduce latency-aware bucketed queue with shelfing to reduce KV-heavy starvation
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: Continuous batcher queues were experiencing starvation of small, latency-sensitive requests when KV-prefetch or KV-heavy requests dominated a shard. This PR introduces a latency-aware bucketed queue with a lightweight 'shelf' mechanism that temporarily demotes high-cost requests but guarantees promotion by aging to avoid indefinite starvation. Key ideas: 1) classify arrivals into latency buckets based on remaining token budget and KV-pin score; 2) place high-cost requests into 'shelves' with a configurable shelf_time_ms and probabilistic promotion probe to keep tail latency bounded; 3) attach kernel-level KV locality hints to requests destined for the same model weights so the scheduler can co-locate compatible batches; 4) implement a soft-timeout steering policy so requests approaching their deadline can be prioritized into a short-lived fast-path coalescer. Changes are conservative and feature-flagged behind scheduler.bucket_shelving.enabled=false by default. Performance: in mixed KV-heavy workloads we see p50 unchanged, p95 reduced by 8% and p99 reduced by 18% on our canary fleet (N=12) compared to the current master scheduler, with no meaningful throughput regression and ~2% lower token compute due to better cache hits. Tests & CI: unit tests for bucket lifecycle and shelf eviction; integration bench harness for mixed workloads added; scheduler bench workflow runs end-to-end on PR level. Rollout plan: staged canary followed by soft enable on Dedicated clusters, monitoring dashboard added to console for shelf occupancy and promotion rates. See release_notes for operator-visible changes.

ci_details: Checks: unit (pass), linters (pass), bench (pass), integration (pass), security-scan (pass). One transient bench timeout rerun fixed by increasing warmup. Total CI runtime ~42m.
release_notes: Operators: enable feature via scheduler.bucket_shelving.enabled=true to activate bucketed queue shelfing. Default is off. New knobs: scheduler.bucket_shelving.shelf_time_ms, scheduler.bucket_shelving.probe_rate, scheduler.bucket_shelving.kv_hints_enabled. Impact: reduces p95/p99 under KV-heavy mixed workloads without throughput regression. Monitor metrics: scheduler.shelf.occupancy, scheduler.shelf.promotion_rate, scheduler.bucket.latency_p95.
bench_results_summary: Canary cluster N=12 mixed workload: p50 ~0% change, p95 -8%, p99 -18%, throughput -0.6% (within noise), token compute -2% due to improved KV cache locality. Full bench harness and raw traces attached to Linear ENG-8421.
notes_for_operators: Feature is opt-in. Start with shelf_time_ms=50, probe_rate=0.05, kv_hints_enabled=false. Observe shelf.promotion_rate and shelf.occupancy for 24h before increasing traffic. Dedicated clusters can tune probe_rate to minimize jitter. If unexpected latency regressions occur, disable scheduler.bucket_shelving.enabled and open ENG-8472.
docs_pointer: docs/ops/scheduler_tuning.md contains rationale, config examples, and troubleshooting checklist.
internal_tests: Added tests: TestBucketLifecycle, TestShelfPromotionAging, TestKVHintNoOpWhenDisabled, IntegrationMixedLatencySmoke. All tests passing locally and on CI.
observability_changes: Added metrics: scheduler_shelf_occupancy, scheduler_shelf_promotion_rate, scheduler_bucket_latency_ms_p95. Console dashboard panel and alert threshold playbook added.
operational_risks: Misconfigured probe_rate can add jitter to latency-sensitive traffic; shelf_time too large can increase queuing for demoted requests. Both parameters are additive and controlled by feature flags so we can roll back quickly.
changelog_entry: Performance: add latency-aware bucketed queue with optional shelfing to reduce KV-induced starvation; feature-gated and off by default.
security_review: No new surface area exposed; KV hints are metadata-only and don't change secrets handling. Security scan passed.
qa_summary: QA ran regression suite (queueing, fault-injection, cold-start). Verified that aging guarantees promotion within configured shelf_time and that KV hints don't alter request routing when disabled.
merge_commit: squash: latency-aware bucketed queue + shelfing (Asha Menon)
